fixes.explanation: Zion is a famous name, so I see why it jumped out. But verse 6 says this regular burnt offering was established at Mount Sinai. Zion just isn't the mountain this verse gives, friend. Sinai is the one.

Grain, baker! Verse 26 says, "On the day of firstfruits, when you present an offering of new grain to the LORD during the Feast of Weeks…" Firstfruits means the first of the new harvest goes to the LORD. As a cookie guy, I respect anything that starts with fresh grain. It also comes with a sacred assembly and no regular work, so that's a day off AND a harvest. Nice.

Seven days, friend! Verse 12 says, "…you shall observe a feast to the LORD for seven days." That matches the feast after Passover (Numbers 28:17). Seven whole days of feasting. Now that's a party I'd need extra cookie boxes for. And hold onto that thought, because verse 35 has one more day waiting at the end.

False, and you caught it! Verse 35 says, "On the eighth day you are to hold a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work." So you finish seven days of feast, you think you're heading back to work, and the text says, "Hold on, one more." I'd take that deal every time. Eight days, and the work can wait.

Guilt and ordination offerings sound serious, and I get why you went there. But verse 39 says these scheduled offerings come "…in addition to your vow and freewill offerings…" That pair is about what people choose to bring on their own, on top of the calendar. The ones you picked just aren't in that verse. So the calendar is the set schedule, and vow and freewill offerings are the extras people give from the heart.
